## Create a table with diversity indexes

```{r}
# Create a table with diversity indexes for the phyloseq object
table <- estimate_richness(ps_cultivar, split = TRUE, measures = NULL)
metadata <- sample_data(ps_cultivar)
merged_table <- cbind(table, metadata)
alfa_diversity_16s <- merged_table
# Specify the path to the new file inside the folder

head(merged_table)  
# Write the table to the Excel file inside the folder

```

## Plot Culture with Wilcoxon test

```{r}
ps_alfa <- ps_cultivar 

Culture_colors <- c(
  "Olive" = "#5A8FBF",
  "Almond" = "#A0522D"
)

# Get the long alpha table used by plot_richness
p_tmp    <- plot_richness(ps_alfa, x = "Culture",
                          measures = c("Chao1","Shannon","Simpson"))
alpha_df <- p_tmp$data

# Compute Wilcoxon p per measure (two levels in Culture)
levs <- levels(droplevels(as.factor(alpha_df$Culture)))
stopifnot(length(levs) == 2)

wilcox_res <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(alpha_df, alpha_df$variable), function(df) {
  df <- df[complete.cases(df$value, df$Culture), ]
  wt <- wilcox.test(value ~ Culture, data = df, exact = FALSE, correct = TRUE)
  data.frame(
    variable    = unique(df$variable),
    p           = wt$p.value,
    group1      = levs[1],
    group2      = levs[2],
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}))

# y-positions per facet and pretty label
y_tops <- aggregate(value ~ variable, alpha_df, function(v) max(v, na.rm = TRUE) * 1.001)
wilcox_res <- merge(wilcox_res, y_tops, by = "variable", all.x = TRUE)
names(wilcox_res)[names(wilcox_res) == "value"] <- "y.position"
wilcox_res$p.label <- scales::label_pvalue(accuracy = 0.001)(wilcox_res$p) # or use p.signif

# Plot with Wilcoxon p annotated (one bracket per facet)
pb1 <- ggplot(alpha_df, aes(x = Culture, y = value, color = Culture)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = NA, width = 0.6, outlier.shape = NA, linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.12, alpha = 0.8, size = 0.9) +  # reduced dot size
  facet_wrap(~ variable, scales = "free_y", nrow = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = Culture_colors, drop = FALSE) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 6) +
  theme(
    strip.text   = element_text(size = 6, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.x  = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5, size = 6),
    axis.text.y  = element_text(size = 5),
    axis.title   = element_text(size = 6),
    panel.spacing = unit(0.2, "lines"),
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.margin = margin(2, 2, 2, 2)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.12))) +
  ggpubr::stat_pvalue_manual(
    wilcox_res,
    label       = "p.label",
    xmin        = "group1",
    xmax        = "group2",
    y.position  = "y.position",
    tip.length  = 0.01,
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size        = 2
  ) +
  labs(x = "", y = NULL)


pb1
# Save the plot to the new directory with specified width, height, and dpi
ggsave(
  filename = file.path(folder_path, "Alfa_diversity_culture_plot.png"),
  plot = pb1,
  width = 3.35, height = 2.0, units = "in",
  dpi = 600,
  device = ragg::agg_png, # crisp text/lines; install.packages("ragg") if needed
  bg = "white"
)

```

## Prepare data - covert to vegan

```{r}

#### Vegan Function to Convert Phyloseq into Something Vegan can call directly
vegan_otu <- function(physeq) {
  OTU <- otu_table(physeq)
  if (taxa_are_rows(OTU)) {
    OTU <- t(OTU)
  }
  return(as(OTU, "matrix"))
}
        
#Convert OTU table to abundance matrix if using Bray-Curtis distance
```

## Plot culture


## Run permanova

```{r}
bray <- phyloseq::distance(ps_beta, method = "bray", weighted = FALSE)
set.seed(42)
adonis_bray <- adonis2(bray ~ factor(Culture), data = vegan_data, permutations = 10000)
print(adonis_bray)
# Save the ADONIS result to a .txt file
writeLines(capture.output(print(adonis_bray)), file.path(folder_path, "Permanova_results_culture.txt"))
```

## 3 - Venn Diagram - Suplementary

## Create a new folder_path

```{r}
folder_path <- "outputs/venn_diagram/"
  if (!dir.exists(folder_path)) {
    dir.create(folder_path, recursive = TRUE)
    cat("Folder created successfully!\n")
  } else {
    cat("Folder already exists!\n")
  }

```

## prepare data - create venn object

```{r}
ps_venn <- ps_cultivar
###################   SHARED AND UNIQUE SEQUENCES BY SITE
        #library(gplots) #required for Venn diagram. Online Venn diagram tools like Venny are also available. 
        
#Empty lists - we have 2 groups so we need 2 empty lists
venn.list<-rep(list(NA),2)
poplist<-rep(list(NA),2)
pops<-as.character(unique(sample_data(ps_venn)$Culture))
          
#Populate List with the Names of Groups we Want to Compare
poplist[[1]]<-pops[1]
poplist[[2]]<-pops[2]

#Name the Groups in the Vennlist
names(venn.list)<-pops


#Loop        
#Loop over each population, subset the phyloseq object to just that population and work out which ASVs are in that population, store those names in the list
        for(k in 1:2){
          
        #Subset Phyloseq Object to One Pop at a time  
         phy.sub<-prune_samples(sample_data(ps_venn)$Culture %in% poplist[[k]],ps_venn)
          
        #Calculate which ASVs are present (non-zero abundance)  
          phy.sub.keep<-apply(otu_table(phy.sub),1,function(x){sum(x)>0})
          
        #Prune down to only those ASVs  
          phy.sub.sub<-prune_taxa(phy.sub.keep,phy.sub)
          
        #Extract the names of these ASVs and store them in the appropriate list slot  
          venn.list[[k]]<-rownames(otu_table(phy.sub.sub))
        } #loop end
        
#Draw Venn Diagram, automatically calculate overlap in the list and unique variants
gplots::venn(venn.list)
```

## Plot

```{r}
venn_culture_colors <- c("#5A8FBF","#A0522D")
ggvenn_plot <- ggvenn(
  venn.list,
  fill_color   = venn_culture_colors,
  stroke_size  = 0.4,         # a bit thinner for small export
  set_name_size = 4,          # set labels (around circles)
  text_size     = 3         # counts inside regions
)

pb_5 <- ggvenn_plot +

  theme(
    plot.title       = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(b = 4)),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    plot.background  = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    axis.text        = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks       = element_blank(),
    axis.title       = element_blank(),
    plot.margin      = margin(t = 12, r = 4, b = 4, l = 4)  # <- more top margin
  )
pb_5
# Save at the same compact size & high DPI as your other figure
ggsave(
  filename = file.path(folder_path, "ggvenn_plot.png"),

  width    = 3.35, height = 2.35, units = "in",
  dpi      = 600,
  device   = ragg::agg_png,
  bg       = "white"
)
```


## prepare data - agregate taxa and agregate rare taxa in "others"

```{r}
taxa <- "Phylum"
#Aggregate rare
ps_aggregate <- microbiome::aggregate_rare(
  ps_tax_comp, level = taxa,
  detection = 0.01, prevalence = 0/100 
)

```

## Save as dataframe

```{r}
otutable <- phyloseq::otu_table(ps_aggregate)
taxtable <- phyloseq::tax_table(ps_aggregate)
sampledata <- phyloseq::sample_data(ps_aggregate)
merged_otu_tax <- merge(taxtable, otutable, by = "row.names")
rownames(merged_otu_tax) <- merged_otu_tax$Row.names
merged_otu_tax <- merged_otu_tax %>%
  dplyr::select(-Row.names)
merged_otu_tax <- t(merged_otu_tax)
merged_otu_tax_sam <- merge(merged_otu_tax, sampledata, by = "row.names")
file_path <- file.path(folder_path, "taxa_relative_frequencies.csv")
head(merged_otu_tax_sam)
write.csv(merged_otu_tax_sam, file_path, row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
sampledata <- phyloseq::sample_data(ps_aggregate)
merged_otu_tax <- merge(taxtable, otutable, by = "row.names")
rownames(merged_otu_tax) <- merged_otu_tax$Row.names
merged_otu_tax <- merged_otu_tax %>%
  dplyr::select(-Row.names)
merged_otu_tax <- t(merged_otu_tax)
merged_otu_tax_sam <- merge(merged_otu_tax, sampledata, by = "row.names")
file_path <- file.path(folder_path, "taxa_relative_frequencies.csv")
head(merged_otu_tax_sam)
write.csv(merged_otu_tax_sam, file_path, row.names = FALSE)
```

## 5 - Faprotax

## Create a new folder_path

```{r}
folder_path <- "outputs/faprotax/"
  if (!dir.exists(folder_path)) {
    dir.create(folder_path, recursive = TRUE)
    cat("Folder created successfully!\n")
  } else {
    cat("Folder already exists!\n")
  }
  
```

## Define my ps object

```{r}
ps_faprotax <- ps_cultivar
ps_faprotax
```

```{r}
faprotax_data <- read.table("data/functional_table.tsv", sep = "\t", header = TRUE, check.names = FALSE)
head(faprotax_data)

# Set 'group' as row names
rownames(faprotax_data) <- faprotax_data$group

# Remove the 'group' column (which is now redundant)
faprotax_data <- faprotax_data[, -1]

sample_data <- as.data.frame(sample_data(ps_faprotax))
sampledata_df2 <- as.data.frame(as.matrix(sample_data))%>%
                    dplyr::rename(Plot = Site)  %>%
                    dplyr::select(-Cultivar_system, -Type, -Tillage, -Animal)
```

## Run deseq

```{r}
cols_keep <- c("A1", "A19", "A2", "A20", "A21", "A22", "A23", "A24", "A3", "A4", "A5", "A6")

faprotax_data <- faprotax_data %>%
  select(any_of(cols_keep))
# 3) Check matching
all(colnames(faprotax_data) == rownames(sampledata_df2))
# should return TRUE

# make sure your colData has the factor in the order you want:
sampledata_df2$Culture <- relevel(factor(sampledata_df2$Culture),
                                       ref = "Almond")

# 4) Create DESeqDataSet
dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
  countData = faprotax_data,
  colData   = sampledata_df2,
  design    = ~ Culture
)

# 5) Run DESeq
dds <- DESeq(dds)

# 6) Extract results
res <- as.data.frame(results(dds, contrast = c("Culture", "Olive", "Almond"))) # c("FACTOR_NAME", "NUMERATOR_LEVEL", "DENOMINATOR_LEVEL")
res_ordered <- res[order(res$padj), ]
# 8. Save results to CSV
write.csv(
  as.data.frame(res_ordered),
  file = file.path(folder_path, "deseq_res.csv")
)

```

## Save results

```{r}
alpha = 0.05
sigtab = res[which(res$padj < alpha), ]
head(sigtab)
sigtab <- sigtab %>%
  arrange(desc(log2FoldChange))

# assuming folder_path is defined, and filename_out is e.g. "sigtab.csv"
filename_out <- "deseq_res_significant.csv"
write.csv(
  sigtab,
  file = file.path(folder_path, filename_out),
  row.names = TRUE
)

```

## Plot deseq complete

```{r}
rownames(sigtab) <- sapply(rownames(sigtab), function(x) {
  # replace underscores with spaces
  x2 <- gsub("_", " ", x)
  # capitalize only the first letter
  paste0(toupper(substr(x2, 1, 1)), substr(x2, 2, nchar(x2)))
})

# 1. Move rownames into a column
sigtab$Function <- rownames(sigtab)

# 2. Create a descriptive Change column
sigtab$Change <- ifelse(
  sigtab$log2FoldChange >= 0,
  "Increased",
  "Decreased"
)

# 3. Preserve current order of functions
sigtab$Function <- factor(sigtab$Function, levels = sigtab$Function)

# 4. Build horizontal barplot with legend and white background
pb4 <- ggplot(sigtab, aes(x = log2FoldChange, y = Function, fill = Change)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    name   = "Olive (Ref Almond)",
    values = c("Increased" = "#5A8FBF", "Decreased" = "#A0522D")
  ) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-2, 2), linetype = "dotted") +
  scale_y_discrete() +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 6) +
  theme(
    axis.text.y   = element_text(size = 5, lineheight = 0.8),
    axis.text.x   = element_text(size = 6),
    axis.title.x  = element_text(size = 6.5, margin = margin(t = 2)),
    axis.title.y  = element_text(size = 6.5, margin = margin(r = 4)),
    plot.title    = element_text(size = 7.5, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    legend.position    = "bottom",
    legend.direction   = "horizontal",
    legend.title       = element_text(size = 6.5),
    legend.text        = element_text(size = 5.5),
    legend.key.size    = unit(5, "pt"),
    legend.key.width   = unit(9, "pt"),
    legend.margin      = margin(0, 0, 0, 0),
    legend.box.margin  = margin(0, 0, 0, 0),
    panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    plot.margin        = margin(3, 4, 3, 4)
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 1, byrow = TRUE, title.position = "top")) +
  labs(
    title = NULL,
    x = "Log2 fold change",
    y = "Putative bacterial functional groups"
  )

  
# 5. Display
print(pb4)

# 6. Save to your folder_path
ggsave(
  filename = file.path(folder_path, "deseq_sig_culture.png"),
  plot     = pb4,
  width = 3.35, height = 2.0, units = "in",
  dpi = 600,
  device = ragg::agg_png, # crisp text/lines; install.packages("ragg") if needed
  bg = "white"
)
```
